exemplar: The passage argues that post-Cold War globalization spread market capitalism and American culture worldwide, but that its benefits were uneven - enriching investors and consumers while displacing workers and provoking cultural backlash.

The North American Free Trade Agreement (1994) lowered trade barriers with Mexico and Canada, accelerating the movement of manufacturing jobs abroad and sparking fierce debate over globalization's costs.

Critics at the 1999 WTO protests in Seattle - labor unions, environmentalists, and human-rights activists - argued that globalization enriched corporations while exploiting workers and degrading the environment.
parts: A. Briefly describe ONE claim the passage makes about globalization in the 1990s.
B. Briefly explain how ONE specific policy or agreement of the 1990s promoted economic globalization.
C. Briefly explain ONE criticism of globalization that emerged by the end of the 1990s.

stimulus.attribution: Original historian-style passage written for this item.
stimulus.text: With the Cold War over, historians argue, the 1990s became the decade of globalization: markets, culture, and information flowed across borders with unprecedented speed. American policymakers promoted free trade, the internet knitted the world together, and multinational corporations operated on every continent. Yet globalization's triumphs were uneven. While consumers enjoyed cheaper goods and investors prospered, manufacturing workers faced plant closings, developing nations struggled with debt and dependency, and critics warned that a single global market was eroding local cultures, labor standards, and the environment.

exemplar: Bradford describes the Pilgrims' arrival as a deliverance: after a perilous ocean crossing, they give thanks to God for bringing them safely to a harbor in the New World.
The Pilgrims fled religious persecution - as Separatists who rejected the Church of England, they first exiled themselves to Holland, then sought a permanent refuge in America.
The colony survived through the help of Native peoples such as Squanto, who taught the settlers to plant corn, and through the Mayflower Compact's framework of self-government.
parts: A. Briefly describe Bradford's account of the Pilgrims' arrival in the excerpt.
B. Briefly explain ONE reason the Pilgrims migrated to New England.
C. Briefly explain ONE factor that helped the Plymouth colony survive its early years.

stimulus.attribution: William Bradford, Of Plymouth Plantation (written c. 1630, published 1856).
stimulus.text: Being thus arrived in a good harbor and brought safe to land, they fell upon their knees and blessed the God of Heaven who had brought them over the vast and furious ocean.
